policies.reason: A conference that adopts a voluntary local action programme. Nothing is required of the city on the date and nothing is measurable after it; a civic goal would score the player against a communique.
An institution replacing an institution. The tariff effects are real and arrive over a decade, so there is no month in which a mayor can be asked what they did about it.
A treaty whose own brief says it does not enter force until 2005. An event that fires eight years before it does anything cannot be resolved in a two-month story cycle.
A capital trend with no date of its own. Booms are the background a city is governed against, not something a council responds to in a given month.
A catastrophe on the other side of the world whose only local surface is warning-system funding. As a civic event it would ask the player to answer for a disaster their city cannot have.
A summit communique. The money it promises reaches a city as public works, and those already fire as their own entries; wrapping the announcement as well would bill the same fact twice.
A declared pandemic that proved milder than the plans written for it. The lasting argument is over stockpile cost after the fact, which has no reading the check can take while it is live.
A West African epidemic whose local surface is port screening. Real, distant and thin — the city's own health capacity is not what the headline is about.
A non-binding target adopted at a conference. Its local weight arrives later through regulation, which is where the story belongs; the signing day is scenery.
Six days of blocked shipping, five months before the supply-chain crunch entry covers the same disruption at the scale a city actually feels. The smaller of two overlapping events.
A treaty signature. The deficit criteria bite on national budgets over years and never name a municipality, so there is no month in which a council answers for them.
A food-safety emergency handled by regulators and an export ban. Nothing a city government does changes any of it, and the mod cannot model food supply at all.
An institution being created. Purely constitutional, severity 2, with no dated local consequence — the rate decisions that matter are separate entries.
An accounting-only currency with no notes in circulation. The 2002 cash changeover is the one households experienced, and it stays.
Two referendums in two member states halting a ratification. A story about the European argument rather than about this city's streets.
The second enlargement in three years, adding nothing to the labour-market question the 2004 accession already puts to the player. Kept in the timeline as history, dropped as a repeat.
Six days of closed airspace. Vivid and genuinely disruptive, but there is no municipal decision inside it — the airline regulator both closed and reopened the sky.
A sentence in a speech that moved bond spreads without a single bond being bought. The austerity conditions it left in force are the 2010 entry's story, not this one's.
Severity 1, and its own brief describes the mood as enlargement fatigue. The least consequential entry in the EU catalog by the catalog's own account.
An election held elsewhere, resolved in a parliament the city is not represented in. The mod already models the player's own elections, and this competes with them for the same attention.
The floor vote before the agreement. NAFTA taking effect three weeks later is the event with consequences, and it stays; wrapping the vote as well doubles one fact.
A market closing at a record. There is nothing to respond to at the top of a boom, and the bust that follows is a separate entry with all the substance in it.

Same day and same subject as the global entry september-11-attacks-2001, which fires in every save including this one. An exact-date duplicate; the global entry is the one that adapts. Consequence, stated rather than left to be discovered: this entry is severity 5 and the surviving twin is severity 4, so in an NA save the wrapped story drops from Mandatory to Major. Accepted — two stories about one morning is worse than one story a tier down, and the NA entry keeps firing as a timeline event at its own severity, unchanged.
Its own brief says the fracking exemption was barely noticed at signature. An event nobody noticed cannot be one a player is scored on noticing.
A movement forming on national television. Party-system flavour with no municipal surface: no service, no price and no district changes on the day.
Dated to the publication of a forecast rather than to anything happening. A projection is not an event, and the price collapse that ends the boom is already its own entry.
Same date and same OPEC decision as the global entry oil-price-collapse-2014. An exact-date duplicate; the global entry is the one that adapts.
A federal withdrawal answered by a mayors' pledge network. The pledge is a press conference — no service, tax or works programme moves in the city because of it.

Same date and same tariffs as the global entry us-china-trade-war-2018. An exact-date duplicate; the global entry is the one that adapts. Same consequence as na-september-11 and stated for the same reason: severity 4 here against 3 on the twin, so in an NA save the wrapped story drops from Major to Minor. Accepted on the same grounds.
A renegotiated agreement signed in 2018 and in force in 2020, keeping continental trade broadly as it was. Procedural, severity 2, and the change it makes is to auto content rules.
Authoring candidate. Fuel, freight and heating bills inside weeks — shield households or hold the budget line is a real choice with a real reading behind it.
Authoring candidate, and the strongest one in the catalog. Severity 5, tax receipts and construction falling together, and bailouts versus services as the argument for a decade.
Authoring candidate. Low-emission zones are a decision a city takes street by street, and the pollution reading answers it honestly.
Authoring candidate. Deferred IT maintenance surfacing as cancelled appointments is a service-coverage story with an obvious goal attached.

Authoring candidate. Severity 5, hospitals and transit and hospitality hit at once, and emergency powers used at a scale a player can be asked to justify.
Authoring candidate, and the most district-dependent entry here: weekday footfall leaves the centre and appears in the outer districts, which is exactly what anyDistrict triggers are for.
Authoring candidate. Municipal running costs jumping mid-budget while wages lag is a cost-of-living story the engine can measure at both ends.
Authoring candidate. Doubled household bills against subsidy, rationing and insulation competing for one budget — three responses, one pot of money.
Authoring candidate. Cooling demand on the grid and an obligation to provide shade, water and cooled public buildings is a services goal with a deadline in it.
Authoring candidate. Tens of thousands of excess deaths among elderly people living alone, and inquiries aimed squarely at emergency planning and elderly care.
Authoring candidate, and district-shaped by construction: the unrest starts on particular estates and the argument is about policing, unemployment and segregated housing.
Authoring candidate. Two weeks without heating gas in midwinter is as concrete as a service failure gets.
Authoring candidate. Austerity as the dominant domestic issue, with national budgets supervised from outside — the clearest alienate-or-enfranchise fork in the EU catalog.
Authoring candidate. Squares occupied over cuts and youth unemployment, with turnout collapsing for governing parties — a direct reading on the player's own position.
Authoring candidate. Severity 5, and every constraint it names — emergency accommodation, school places, relocation — is municipal rather than national.
Authoring candidate. A court clearing cities to ban older diesels is a decision handed to the player, with organised opposition already in the brief.
Authoring candidate. Warning chains and evacuation orders failed at local level, which makes the failure the player's to own.
Authoring candidate. Housing, school places and language provision named in the brief as the binding constraints at municipal level.
Authoring candidate. Heating and lighting limits applied to public buildings is an obligation with a number attached and a visible cost to defying it.
Authoring candidate. Six days of rioting with policing practice and inner-city disinvestment dominating municipal politics afterwards.
Authoring candidate. Responsibility for whoever is left after the caseload falls moves to city services — poverty becoming a municipal service problem, in the brief's own words.
Authoring candidate. Emergency management, evacuation planning and infrastructure maintenance moving from technical questions to electoral ones is the whole premise of the mod.
Authoring candidate. The property-tax base falls with a lag, so the municipal crisis arrives after the national one is declared over — a genuinely two-stage story.
Authoring candidate. Flooded tunnels and substations turning climate adaptation into a capital-budget argument in every exposed city.
Authoring candidate, and the most damning: a cost-driven decision, eighteen months of official denial, and the collapse of trust in technical assurances.
Authoring candidate. Body cameras, consent decrees and fines-and-fees practice are municipal policy the player can be asked to move.
Authoring candidate. Police budgets, use-of-force rules and civilian oversight become ballot-level questions — the alienate-or-enfranchise mechanism with no translation needed.
Authoring candidate. Competitive grants reward cities with the capacity to bid, which is a story about the player's administration rather than about Washington.
Authoring candidate. Worst-on-record air quality with schools closed and outdoor work stopped, on a single dated day.
